aboutBody: The Bulls Head is a relaxed place to meet, have a pint and stay awhile. With cask ale, a garden, live music and a traditional pub atmosphere, the focus is simple: a friendly local that feels easy to walk into.

index.t12: From live music nights and charity days to plenty more exciting events, there is always something to look forward to at The Bulls Head.

index.t08: Four-legged regulars are welcome too, so nobody has to miss out on a visit to the pub.
index.t03: Real ale, a fully enclosed garden, open fires in winter and live music. Back under new management since August 2025.
index.t06: Bidford's story begins at the river. The Roman road known as Ryknild Street once crossed the Avon at a ford near St Laurence's Church. In the early fifteenth century a stone bridge took the crossing farther west. It was already being repaired in 1449, and its eight arches still carry people into the village today.
index.t15: We took over The Bulls Head in August 2025 with a simple vision: to bring the heart and community spirit back into our beautiful traditional village pub.
index.t16: Since then, we’ve been the faces of the pub and working hard behind the scenes. The support we’ve received has been humbling, and seeing the community come together for our charity events has made us especially proud.
index.t17: We’re delighted to have raised £700 for “I’m Homeless Get Me Out of Here”, and we’re proud to support the British Legion Poppy Appeal every year.
index.t18: Our regular acoustic evenings are becoming a favourite with musicians and customers alike, whether they’re playing or joining in with a singalong.
index.t19: The journey hasn’t always been easy, but we’re getting there. We hope to be serving food soon.
index.t20: We’re proud to be the publicans of The Bulls Head, and we look forward to welcoming you.
index.t21: By 1861, Bidford had around 950 residents and a busy High Street. Grocers, butchers and drapers served local households, while farmers, blacksmiths and other trades kept the village working. There were seven pubs and inns in Bidford at the time — and The Bulls Head was one of them.
index.t22: CAMRA records this pub as having served pints for more than 200 years. Generations of shops, trades and neighbours have come and gone around it, but the pub is still here at 36 High Street. It remains somewhere to meet after work, catch up with friends and take part in the life of the village.

visit.t03: The Bulls Head is at 36 High Street, right in the centre of Bidford-on-Avon. The 247 Stratford–Redditch and 28 Stratford–Evesham bus services stop close by.
